At SIM3 Level 0, this is the state of the response process when a malicious scheduled task is confirmed: there isn't one.
At SIM3 Level 1, analysts informally know how to respond to a scheduled-task incident, but nothing is written down.
At SIM3 Level 2, a written runbook exists covering containment and eradication steps for scheduled-task persistence incidents.
At SIM3 Level 3, the runbook includes automation hooks like auto-disabling the task or auto-isolating the host, and is kept current.
At SIM3 Level 4, the runbook and its automation are periodically audited against real incidents to confirm they still work.
At SAMM Level 0, this is the control restricting who can create scheduled tasks on domain-joined systems: none exists.
At SAMM Level 1, scheduled task creation is restricted by local policy on some systems, but inconsistently applied.
At SAMM Level 2, an org-wide documented policy and GPO restrict task creation to approved service accounts, reviewed periodically.
At SAMM Level 3, the control is enforced via centrally managed policy-as-code, monitored for drift, and tied to an effectiveness metric.
At this stretch level, the control is continuously reassessed and re-architected as adversary use of scheduled tasks evolves.
